en: And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: al-Mula'i narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, with this chain of narration, and he added: 'And I have not heard anyone other than him say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, who said: I heard Jundab al-Alaqi say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever seeks to make people hear of his deeds, Allah will make him heard of in disgrace; and whoever shows off, Allah will expose him.'

Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Ismail ibn Sumay', from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever seeks fame and reputation, Allah will make him heard of; and whoever shows off, Allah will expose him.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Rawh ibn al-Qasim informed us, from al-Ala ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: I am the Most Self-Sufficient, having no need of associates. Whoever performs a deed wherein he associates anyone else along with Me, I abandon him and his association.'

And Ahmad ibn Abdah ad-Dabbi narrated it to us: Abu Dawud informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salama narrated to us: Wahb ibn Kaysan narrated to us, with this chain of narration, except that he said: 'And I allocate one-third of it to the needy, the beggars, and the wayfarer.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is that of Abu Bakr—both saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salama narrated to us, from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said: 'While a man was in a barren wilderness of land, he heard a voice in a cloud saying: Water the garden of so-and-so! That cloud moved aside and poured its water over a volcanic stony plain (harrah). Behold, one of those watercourses had contained all that water. He followed the water, and behold, there was a man standing in his garden directing the water with his shovel. He said to him: O servant of Allah, what is your name? He said: So-and-so—mentioning the very name he had heard in the cloud. The man said to him: O servant of Allah, why do you ask me about my name? He said: I heard a voice in the cloud whose water this is, saying: Water the garden of so-and-so! mentioning your name; so what do you do with it? He said: Since you have said this: I look at what comes out of it, and I give one-third of it in charity, I and my dependents eat one-third, and I return one-third back into it.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Zayd ad-Dili, who said: I heard Abu al-Ghayth narrating from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who looks after an orphan, whether related to him or not, I and he will be like these two in Paradise.' And Malik gestured with his index finger and middle finger.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said: 'The one who strives on behalf of the widow and the poor is like the warrior in the cause of Allah'—and I think he said—'and like the one who stands in night prayer without tiring, and like the fasting person who never breaks his fast.'

And Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to us: Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us: Ubaydullah narrated to me, with this chain of narration, the like of it, except that he said: 'They drew water from its wells and kneaded dough with it.'

Al-Hakam ibn Musa Abu Salih narrated to me: Shu'ayb ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Ubaydullah informed us, from Nafi, that Abdullah ibn Umar informed him that the people halted with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) at al-Hijr, the land of Thamud, and drew water from its wells and kneaded dough with it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) commanded them to pour out the water they had drawn, to feed the dough to the camels, and commanded them to draw water from the well which the she-camel used to frequent.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab—as he mentioned al-Hijr, the dwellings of Thamud—Salim ibn Abdillah said that Abdullah ibn Umar said: We passed by al-Hijr along with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to us: 'Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves unless you are weeping, lest there befall you the like of what befell them.' Then he spurred his mount and sped up until he left it behind.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutayba ibn Sa'id, and Ali ibn Hujr all narrated to us from Ismail—Ibn Ayyub said: Ismail ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Dinar informed me that he heard Abdullah ibn Umar saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said concerning the people of al-Hijr: 'Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping; and if you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest there befall you the like of what befell them.'

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Abu Hani informed me that he heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli saying: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As when a man asked him, saying: 'Are we not among the poor Emigrants (al-Muhajirun)?' Abdullah said to him: 'Do you have a wife to whom you return?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you have a home in which you dwell?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then you are among the wealthy.' The man said: 'I also have a servant.' He said: 'Then you are among the kings.' Abu Abd al-Rahman said: And three persons came to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As while I was with him, and said: 'O Abu Muhammad, by Allah, we have nothing: neither provision, nor riding animal, nor belongings.' He said to them: 'It is as you wish: if you wish, you may return to us and we will give you whatever Allah facilitates for you; if you wish, we will mention your situation to the ruler; and if you wish, you may endure with patience, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: The poor Emigrants will precede the rich into Paradise on the Day of Resurrection by forty autumns (years).' They said: 'Then we shall be patient and ask for nothing.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna—both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard an-Nu'man delivering a sermon, saying: Umar mentioned what the people had acquired of worldly wealth, and said: 'I indeed saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) spending the entire day twisting in hunger, not finding even poor-quality dates (daqal) with which to fill his stomach.'

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us. (And via another chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: al-Mula'i informed us: Isra'il narrated to us, both from Simak, with this chain of narration, similar to it; and in the hadith of Zuhayr he added: 'And yet you are not satisfied with anything less than various sorts of dates and butter.'

Qutayba ibn Sa'id and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, both saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, who said: I heard an-Nu'man ibn Bashir saying: 'Are you not enjoying food and drink as much as you wish? I indeed saw your Prophet (peace be upon him) not finding enough poor-quality dates to fill his stomach.' And Qutayba did not mention 'with it'.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan: Abu Hazim narrated to me, who said: I saw Abu Hurayrah gesturing repeatedly with his finger, saying: 'By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Abu Hurayrah, the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) and his family never ate their fill of wheat bread for three consecutive days until he departed from this world.'

Muhammad ibn Abbad and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, both saying: Marwan—meaning al-Fazari—narrated to us, from Yazid—and he is Ibn Kaysan—from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: 'By the One in Whose hand is my soul'—and Ibn Abbad said: 'By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Abu Hurayrah'—'the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) never satisfied his family with wheat bread for three consecutive days until he departed from this world.'

And Abu Kurayb narrated to us: al-Ashja'i narrated to us. (And via another chain) Nasr ibn Ali narrated to us: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, both from Sufyan, with this chain of narration, except that in their hadith from Sufyan: 'And we never ate our fill of the two black things (dates and water).'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur ibn Safiyyah, from his mother, from Aisha, who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) passed away when we had had our fill of the two black things: water and dates.'

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Dawud ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makki al-Attar informed us, from Mansur, from his mother, from Aisha. (And via another chain) Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us: Dawud ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Attar narrated to us: Mansur ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hajabi narrated to me, from his mother Safiyyah, from Aisha, who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) passed away at the time when people had eaten their fill of the two black things: dates and water.'

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad narrated to me: Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Yazid ibn Abdillah ibn Qusayt. (And via another chain) Harun ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Ibn Qusayt, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) died without ever having eaten his fill of bread and olive oil twice in a single day.'

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-Ala ibn Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) passed away when there was nothing on my shelf that a living creature could eat except a small portion of barley on a shelf of mine. I ate from it until a long time had passed for me, so I measured it, whereupon it was soon exhausted.'

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us, from his father, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Urwah, from Aisha, that she used to say: 'By Allah, O son of my sister, we would sight the crescent, then the crescent, then the crescent—three crescents in two months—without a fire ever being kindled in the houses of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).' He said: I said: 'O maternal aunt, what sustained you?' She said: 'The two black things: dates and water, except that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) had neighbors among the Ansar who possessed milch animals, and they would send some of their milk to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and he would give it to us to drink.'

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Abu Usama and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, with this chain of narration: 'We would remain...' and he did not mention 'the family of Muhammad.' And Abu Kurayb added in his hadith from Ibn Numayr: 'unless a little meat was brought to us.'

Amr an-Naqid narrated to us: Abda ibn Sulayman narrated to us; he said: and Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, who said: 'We, the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him), would remain for a month without kindling a fire, having nothing except dates and water.'

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Hilal ibn Humayd, from Urwah, from Aisha, who said: 'The family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) never ate their fill of wheat bread for two consecutive days without one of those days having only dates.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, who said: Aisha said: 'The family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) never ate their fill of wheat bread for three days until he passed away.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, from his father, from Aisha, who said: 'The family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) never ate their fill of wheat bread for more than three days.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid narrating from al-Aswad, from Aisha, that she said: 'The family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) never ate their fill of barley bread for two consecutive days until the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was taken.'
